Revised assessment using the Financial Stability Report (FSR) lens:
- Core message remains supportive: activity and employment strengthening, policy highly accommodative (0–0.25% fed funds range, ongoing QE), and taper flagged as “soon” conditional on continued progress. Forward guidance aims to anchor inflation expectations around 2%.
- FSR context tempers the positivity: the Fed’s FSR highlights elevated asset valuations and compressed risk premiums amid very low rates, pockets of vulnerability in nonbank financial intermediation and run‑prone funding vehicles, and sectoral risks (notably CRE/CMBS). These vulnerabilities could amplify shocks if conditions tighten or virus-related setbacks persist.
- Offsetting FSR positives: banks remain well capitalized and liquid; credit flows to households and businesses are solid; supervisory and stress-testing posture remains vigilant; policy tools and facilities underpin market functioning.

Net effect: still mildly positive but closer to neutral after incorporating the FSR’s vulnerability assessment.
